note: GB-82. Snapshot lease status as the production lease table answers it (snapshot.rs Leases::status behind SNAPSHOT_LEASE_STATUS). Each case is an ordered list of steps run against one lease table; a `query` step names the (snapshot, handle) asked about and the state the broker answers. A handle covers its own lease and every `<handle>#<suffix>` lease; a handle that was never held, a prefix of a handle, and a different suffix are UNKNOWN; REAPED needs a durable completion that outlives the process (`restart` builds a new table on the same directory). The answer echoes the queried snapshot and ownership: {type:SNAPSHOT_LEASE_STATUS, schema:rustright.snapshot-lease-status.v1, state, snapshot, ownership}. A fake broker must answer UNKNOWN, not REAPED, for a lease that was never held, and keep completed and never-held apart. GB-23: the answer also carries `members`, one row {handle,state,spawned,refused,job} per submission the broker knows under the queried handle (the handle itself or any `<handle>#...`), sorted by handle; `state` of the answer is only the aggregate: REAPED requires every member REAPED and at least one member, so a completed sibling never stands in for a claimed submission without a completion (a start that may have run: op `unknown-start`) or for a lease record that still stands. A client that recorded sub-handles reconciles each against `members`; a recorded sub-handle absent from `members` never reached the broker and is the client's own no-submit evidence, never a REAPED.

cases.name: a never-held handle is UNKNOWN, a held one ACTIVE, a completed one REAPED, durably
a lease that ran nothing and was never held stays UNKNOWN
a completed sibling never stands in for an unknown submission (GB-23)
a refused handle is a settled member that ran nothing (GB-23, GB-25)
